case.title: Your home doesn’t fit in a number
case.note: Personal project with a fictional brand, created to show how I approach a consideration video. Voiceover in Portuguese.
case.lead: A consideration video for people who already know Nimbo and are comparing providers. Instead of competing on speed, it changes the question: the right internet depends on the home’s layout, the routine of the people who live there and the support when you need it.
facts: People who know the brand and are comparing providers
Vertical motion design · 45 s · voiceover and captions
strategy: If every provider sells fiber and high speeds, Nimbo enters the race by looking at what the others ignore: rooms, routines and support.
Talks about the router, Wi-Fi and setup from the resident’s point of view: where the device goes and what each room needs.
No price, no “sign up now”. Nimbo shows up as a way of thinking about the choice, to make the shortlist of people who are deciding.
scenes: The right question: your home doesn’t fit in a number
Beyond speed: megabits matter, but they’re not everything
Rooms: the floor plan changes the Wi-Fi path
Support: help is part of the choice too
The Nimbo view: the home first, then the plan
Sign-off: your home before the megabits

items: people who stayed until Nimbo showed its way of thinking
people who reached the brand sign-off
a sign the new criteria made sense
survey: which providers would you consider?
people who went to look on their own, unprompted
customers talk about their home, not just speed
metrics.note: Consideration is measured by comparing people who saw the video with people who didn’t. The plan starts from a baseline and tests one change at a time.

case.why: When everyone competes on speed, whoever changes the question gets ahead.
